title: Private Photo Platform
outcome: Live in production: guests see only the photos a manager links them to; selfie matches never grant access.
summary: Wedding guests had no private, easy way to find the photos they appear in. A live wedding website, now in production, combines SMS sign-in, guest uploads, manager moderation and an AI photo album that groups faces into people for the couple to link to guests. Face recognition is designed as an explicit opt-in.
cv: Side project outside the CV roles: a production web platform, self-hosted end to end.

cards.title: Each guest sees only their photos
cards.caption: Guests sign in with an SMS code, then browse a gallery filtered to what their access allows. Photos: Wikimedia Commons, CC0 / CC BY, see credits.
cards.alt: Guest photo gallery of a sample wedding with a caption bar explaining visibility

cards.title: AI faces: "Who is this?"
cards.caption: Faces detected by InsightFace are clustered into people in pgvector. A manager links each person to a guest, ranked by similarity, or hides bystanders. Photos: Wikimedia Commons, CC0 / CC BY, see credits.
cards.alt: Face review dialog listing guests with similarity percentages for an unnamed person

cards.title: Architecture
cards.caption: Astro SSR web and a Fastify API over Postgres with pgvector, a headless Immich backend for storage and face detection, and Twilio Verify for sign-in, self-hosted behind a Cloudflare Tunnel.
cards.alt: Architecture diagram: guest and manager, Cloudflare Tunnel, Astro web, Fastify API, Postgres, Immich, Twilio, and a six-step face pipeline

cards.title: One access rule, in SQL
cards.caption: The single visibility predicate: a guest sees a photo only if a manager linked them to a face in it, or granted them its category. Selfie matches never grant access.

cards.title: Engineering discipline
cards.caption: Counted from the repository: decision records, design specs, test files and API modules. CI checks format, lint ratchet, types, tests and build on every push.

cards.title: Walkthrough
cards.caption: 28 seconds of the real web build: gallery, people pages and face review. Sample photos from Wikimedia Commons, fictional names.

description.text: Silent, 28 seconds, with an on-screen caption bar. 0:00 The wedding site for Alex and Jordan shows a photo gallery. Caption: "Guests sign in with their phone" (Twilio Verify one-time code, then a secure session cookie). 0:05 The gallery scrolls through photos. Caption: "The gallery shows only what this guest may see": all-guest photos, photos they are in, and categories they were granted. 0:10 The People page shows round face thumbnails with names. Caption: "People: face clusters linked to guests". Guests can browse everyone, and their own cluster shows as "Me". 0:15 A person page for Jordan Morgan lists their photos. 0:18 The admin Manage wedding screen opens the face review. Caption: "Faces: Who is this?" The admin links a face cluster to a guest, merges look-alikes and hides bystanders.

cards.title: Built with Claude Code
cards.body: Built spec first with Claude Code: 12 specs, agent instructions kept in the repo, test-first house rules and CI gates. Privacy rules were recorded as decision records. The same instruction files work with GitHub Copilot agent mode.
